newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Utd Biscuits says UK margins up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Utd Biscuits says UK margins up.

text.p: United Biscuits (Holdings) Plc said efforts to revitalise profit growth are on track, with first half profits and margins ahead in the UK, its biggest market in terms of sales.
Chief executive Eric Nicoli said profits were up 12 percent in the UK, despite the pressures on UK food business and margins were up too.
"Margin is rebuilding and we're seeing growth in all of our businesses in the UK," he said in a telephone interview.
Nicoli said margins in UK biscuits and snacks were up by just under one percentage point to 9.4 percent and the margin in frozen food up modestly to seven percent.
Returns on capital employed were now 20 percent plus in the UK businesses, the chief executive said.
Last year the group got out of its loss-making Keebler business in the U.S. and its Spanish snacks business at considerable cost.
"What we committed to doing this year was to return to growth and to deliver a substantial profit improvement...and we think these results reflect that," Nicoli said.

Profits in Europe were down 30 percent, but this was an improvement on a steep decline in the second half of last year. Nicoli said UB fully expected continental Europe to finish the year ahead of last year's performance.
In Asia, sales were up nearly 30 percent. But in Australia he said the snacks business bought three years ago was under attack from rival PepsiCo. Profits fell to A$5 million from A$7 million.
"But we fully expect to deal with the competitive attack and produce a respectable level of profit for the full year," Nicoli said.
He expressed confidence in the group's strategy to restore overall profit growth by focusing on its existing businesses and keeping costs down. "The recovery is really underway," he said.
On dividend policy, Nicoli said the group intended to increase the payout as soon as was sensible.
"We've always said our medium term objective is to have (dividend) cover of two but no one should be concerned that we won't move it until we have cover of two," he said.
UB reported first half pretax profits of 44.9 million stg before exceptional charges, up from 22.9 million last year.
The group held its dividend at 3.5 pence.
